slos.description:
define the following:
a. amplitude,
b. frequency,
c. oscillatory motion
d. periodic motion,
e. time period;
discuss the factors on which the time period of a simple pendulum depends;
solve word problems related to time period of a simple pendulum;
define mechanical waves;
describe wave motion as illustrated by vibrations in rope, a slinky spring and by experiments with water waves;
describe that waves transfer energy without transferring matter;
identify transverse and longitudinal waves in mechanical media;
distinguish between mechanical and electromagnetic waves;

define the following terms:
a. speed (v),
b. wavelength (λ),
c. crest,
d. trough,
e. wavefront,
f. compression and rarefaction;
analyse key characteristics of waves by interpreting graphical representations of waveforms;
derive equation v = f λ;
solve word problems using the relation f = 1/ T and v = f λ;

define the following terms:
a. reflection,
b. refraction,
c. diffraction;
describe the properties of waves such as reflection, refraction and diffraction with the help of the ripple tank effect.
explain the production of sound waves;
explain that sound waves cannot travel in a vacuum;
describe that the speed of sound depends upon the physical characteristic of a medium;
describe the longitudinal nature of sound waves;
state audible frequency range;
define the terms ‘pitch’, ‘loudness’ and ‘quality of sound’;
describe graphically the effect of changes in amplitude on loudness and the effect of changes in frequency on the pitch of sound;
define the intensity of sound and state its SI unit;
describe the intensity level of sound and mention its unit;
solve word problems related to the intensity level of sound;
describe an echo as the reflection of sound waves;
describe simple experiments to show the reflection of sound waves;
examine a method involving a measurement of distance and time for determining the speed of sound in air;
describe infrasound with examples;
describe ultrasound with examples;
describe the importance of acoustic protection;
analyse the effects of noise pollution on the environment.

describe with reference to the reflection of light the following
terms:
a. normal,
b. angle of incidence,
c. angle of reflection;
state laws of reflection of light;

discuss the relationship of the position of an object with the
characteristics of image formed by a plane mirror;

describe with reference to the refraction of light the following
terms:
a. angle of incidence,
b. angle of refraction,
c. refractive index;
state laws of refraction of light;

solve word problems of refractive index using the given formulae:
a. sin ∠i/ sin ∠r,
b. speed of light in vacuum/ speed of light in the given medium,
c. real depth/ apparent depth;

illustrate the passage of light ray through parallel-sided
transparent material (glass slab);
illustrate the passage of light through a glass prism;
explain the dispersion of light by a prism;
explain the scattering of light by the molecules in the air;

state the traditional seven colours of the visible spectrum in
order of frequency and in order of wavelength;
define total internal reflection;
state the conditions necessary for total internal reflection;
describe the relation between critical angle and refractive index;
solve word problems related to the critical angle and refractive index;
illustrate the action of thin converging and thin diverging lenses on a parallel beam of light;
draw images by placing objects at different positions in front of convex and concave lens;
differentiate between real and virtual images;
solve word problems related to the image location by lenses using lens formula;
define power of a lens and state its unit;
define magnifying power of lens;
define least distance of distinct vision;
describe the use of a single lens (magnifying glass) with its ray diagram;
define short-sightedness and long-sightedness;

draw ray diagrams to show the formation of images in the eye of an individual with reference to:
a. normal vision,
b. short-sightedness,
c. long-sightedness;
describe the correction of short-sightedness and long-sightedness using concave and convex lenses;

define the following:
a. acoustic lensing,
b. gravitational lensing.
define charge and its types;
describe electric charge as an integral multiple of elementary charge (electron);
explain that charging of solids by friction involves only a transfer of negative charge (electrons);
describe production and detection of electric charge;
state that unlike charges attract and like charges repel;
explain Coulomb’s law;
solve word problems related to the electrostatic charges by using Coulomb’s law;
describe the process of electrostatic induction;
explain charging of a conductor by electrostatic induction;
describe the application of electrostatics in electrostatic precipitator and photocopier;
explain the process of lightning in atmosphere during thunderstorms;

identify different kinds of electrical lightning includes:
a. ball lightning,
b. elves,
c. ghosts,
d. jets,
e. pixies,
f. sprites,
g. trolls;
define electric field and electric field intensity;
describe that the direction of an electric field line at a point is the direction of the force exerted on a positive charge at that point;

draw electric field lines for:
a. an isolated positive charge,
b. an isolated negative point charge,
c. two-point charges having opposite charge,
d. two-point charges having identical charge;

explain phenomenon of electrical breakdown with its practical application in:
a. corona discharge ozone generator
b. gas discharge lamp,
c. lightning rod,
d. plasma display;
define electric current;
differentiate between conventional and non-conventional current;
differentiate between direct current (D.C.) and alternating current (A.C.);
solve word problems related to electric current using $I = \frac{Q}{t}$;
distinguish between conductors and insulators;
describe electrical conduction in metals in terms of the movement of free electrons;
define resistance and resistivity with its SI unit;

describe the following factors affecting the resistance of a metallic conductor: a. length of a conductor, b. cross-sectional area of a conductor, c. nature of a conductor, d. temperature of a conductor;
describe the phenomenon of superconductivity in solids;
describe the action of negative temperature coefficient (NTC) in thermistors and light dependent resistors;
define potential difference
solve word problems related to potential difference using $V = \frac{\mathrm{work}}{q}$;
compare potential difference and electromotive force;
state that the e.m.f. of identical power sources connected in parallel is equal to the e.m.f. of one of the sources;
calculate the total e.m.f. where several power sources are arranged in series;
state Ohm’s law with its limitations;
interpret the I-V characteristics graph for a fixed resistor, a filament lamp and a thermistor;
define electrical power;
explain Joule’s law in terms of energy dissipated in the resistor;
solve word problems related to E = IVt = I2Rt = V 2 t / R ;
calculate the total energy cost based on the cost price of kWh;
state the use of electrical measuring devices; (galvanometer, ammeter and voltmeter)
describe the functions of live, neutral and earth wires in the domestic main power supply;
state common uses of electricity; (including heating, lighting, battery charging and powering motors and electronic systems);

describe common electric hazards that can result from malpractice and lack of maintenance; (damaged insulation, overheating cables, damp conditions, excess current from overloading of plugs, extension leads, single and multiple sockets when using a main supply);
explain the importance of connecting domestic (A.C.) supplies in parallel;
describe the usage of A.C. in daily life (switches, fuses, circuit breakers);
explain the safety measures in household electricity.

subtopics.name: Series and Parallel Combination of Resistance

slos.description: describe the characteristics of series and parallel combinations of resistors;
derive the effective/ equivalent resistance of resistors connected in series and in parallel;
calculate the effective/ equivalent resistance of resistors connected in series, parallel and both;
define electric circuits;

draw the circuit diagrams of the following electrical components:
a. ammeters,
b. batteries,
c. cells,
d. diodes,
e. fuses,
f. lamps,
g. light-dependent resistors (LDRs),
h. light-emitting diodes (LEDs),
i. resistors (fixed and variable),
j. switches,
k. thermistors (NTC only),
l. voltmeters;
calculate current, voltage, power and resistance in parts of a circuit or in the whole circuit that includes three resistors.
define magnetic and non-magnetic substances;
state domain theory of magnetism;
explain magnetisation and demagnetisation of materials in light of domain theory;
define diamagnetic, paramagnetic and ferromagnetic solids;
compare soft and hard ferromagnetic materials;
describe uses of permanent magnets and electromagnets;
define the forces acting between magnetic poles and those between magnets and magnetic materials;
describe the direction of the magnetic field of a magnet at a point;
describe magnetic fields and magnetic lines of forces between the two poles of a magnet;
compare strong and weak magnetic fields;
define magnetic flux;
explain the formation of the Earth’s magnetic field;

subtopics.name: Magnetic Field by Current Carrying Conductor

slos.description: describe the pattern and direction of the magnetic field due to currents in straight wires and in solenoids;
describe the effect of changing the magnitude and direction of the current on the magnetic field;

subtopics.name: Current Carrying Conductor in a Magnetic Field

slos.description: show that a magnetic force acts on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field;
state Fleming’s left-hand rule;
describe the effect on the magnetic force of reversing the direction of current and magnetic field;
describe the magnetic field patterns between parallel current carrying conductors and relate these to the forces on the conductors;
describe that a current carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a torque with the help of Fleming’s left-hand rule;

describe the turning effect is increased by increasing the:
a. area of a coil,
b. electric current,
c. number of turns on the coil,
d. strength of the magnetic field;
describe construction and working of a D.C. motor.
describe that a changing magnetic field can induce electromotive force (e.m.f.) in a wire or coil;

subtopics.name: Faraday’s Law of Electromagnetic Induction and Lenz’s Law

slos.description: state Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction;
describe Lenz’s law, setup an experiment to show that an e.m.f. induces with in a coil opposes the change that produces it;
describe the simple construction and working of an A.C. generator;
interpret graphs of e.m.f. against time for simple A.C. generators;
define self-induction;
define mutual induction;
describe inductance;
describe the construction and the principle of operation of a simple iron-cored transformer;
state the two types of transformers and their uses;
discuss the application of transformer in high voltage transmission;
solve word problem using the transformer equation $\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{I_p}{I_s} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}$;
describe the production, transmission and reception of electromagnetic (EM) waves;
describe the main regions of the electromagnetic spectrum in order of frequency and order of wavelength with their applications;
describe the damages caused by electromagnetic radiation;
explain the process of thermionic emission emitted from a filament;
describe the simple construction and use of an electron gun as a source of electron beam;
describe the effect of electric and magnetic field on an electron beam;
describe the basic principle and uses of CRO and make a list of its uses;
interpret waveforms on oscilloscopes;
explain the importance of electronics;
compare analogue and digital electronics;
state Boolean algebra;
convert decimal numbers into binary numbers;
state the basic operations of digital electronics;
identify and make the symbols for the logic gates; (NOT, OR, AND, NOR and NAND)
state the action of logic gates in truth table form with two inputs;
use universal gates (NAND and NOR) to create NOT, OR and AND;
describe the uses of logic gates.

describe that the alpha particle scattering experiments provide evidence for:
a. a very small nucleus surrounded by mostly empty space,
b. a nucleus containing most of the mass of the atom,
c. a nucleus that is positively charged;
describe the composition of the nucleus of an atom in terms of protons and neutrons;
explain that the number of protons in a nucleus distinguishes one element from the other;
show various nuclides by using the symbol of proton number (Z), nucleon number (A) and the nuclide notation (X);
define isotopes;
state that an element may have more than one isotope;

describe the uses of isotopes in:
a. diagnosis and treatment of cancer,
b. household fire (smoke) alarms,
c. irradiating food to kill bacteria,
d. measuring and controlling thicknesses of materials,
e. sterilisation of equipment;
define radioactivity;
explain that some nuclei are unstable;
describe the spontaneous and random emission of radiation from a nucleus;
describe the properties of the three types of radiation (α, β and γ);
explain that an element may change into another element when radioactivity occurs;
show changes in the composition of a nucleus by symbolic equations when alpha or beta particles are emitted from it;
explain the existence of background radiation;

state the sources that make a significant contribution to the background radiation including:
a. cosmic rays,
b. food and drinks,
c. radon gas (in the air),
d. rocks and buildings;
explain half-life of a radioactive material;
calculate the half-life of radioactive elements;
draw graphs showing decay curves of these elements;
describe the process of carbon dating to estimate the age of ancient objects;
describe nuclear fission and fusion reactions;
calculate the energy released in the process of nuclear reaction using the equation E = mc2;
state the nature of the Sun consisting mostly of hydrogen and helium and radiates most of its energy;
state the effects of ionising nuclear radiations on living things, including cell death, mutations and cancer;

explain that radioactive materials are moved, used and stored in a safe way, with reference to:
a. reducing exposure time,
b. using shield to absorb radiation,
c. increasing distance between source and living tissue;
